**12.3 Meetings and Notice**
The LPAC shall meet at least **quarterly** (i.e., at least four times per year). The General Partner shall provide at least **15 business days\'** advance written notice of each LPAC meeting, together with an agenda and any materials to be considered. Meetings may be held in person or by video or telephone conference. The General Partner may call special meetings of the LPAC upon reasonable notice.
**[Section 13: Excuse and Exclusion]{.underline}**
**13.1 Excuse Rights**
A Limited Partner may request to be excused from participating in a particular investment if such participation would cause (a) a **regulatory violation** applicable to such Limited Partner, (b) a **tax penalty** imposed on such Limited Partner, or (c) a **conflict** with such Limited Partner\'s governing documents or published investment policies.
The General Partner shall have **sole discretion** to grant or deny excuse requests, subject to its obligation to act in **good faith**. For the avoidance of doubt, the LPAC shall have no approval right with respect to excuse requests.
**13.2 Effect of Excuse on Management Fees and Commitments**
Excused amounts shall **not** reduce the excused Limited Partner\'s capital commitment for any purpose under the LPA, including for purposes of **management fee calculation**. Accordingly, a Limited Partner that is excused from a particular investment shall continue to pay management fees on its full capital commitment (including the excused amount). Excused amounts are **not** subject to recycling by the General Partner.
**13.3 Reallocation of Excused Amounts**
The share of an excused Limited Partner in the relevant investment shall be reallocated **pro rata** among the non-excused Limited Partners (not to the General Partner). No Limited Partner shall be required to fund more than its unfunded commitment as a result of such reallocation.
**[Section 14: Co-Investment]{.underline}**
**14.1 Co-Investment Opportunities**
The General Partner shall offer co-investment opportunities to Limited Partners (and their affiliates) **before** offering such opportunities to third parties. Allocation of co-investment opportunities shall be determined by the General Partner in its **sole discretion**, subject to LPAC oversight (as provided in Section 12.2(b)).
**No management fee or carried interest** shall be charged on co-investments, unless otherwise agreed in a co-investment vehicle side letter. The General Partner shall notify Limited Partners of available co-investment opportunities within **5 business days** of the Fund\'s commitment to the relevant investment.
**[Section 15: Reporting]{.underline}**
**15.1 Quarterly Reports**
The General Partner shall provide to each Limited Partner unaudited financial statements and a portfolio summary within **60 days** after the end of each fiscal quarter. Quarterly reports shall include: (a) Fund-level financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement); (b) portfolio company summaries (including investment cost, current fair value, and key operating metrics); (c) capital account statements for each Limited Partner; (d) subscription line utilization; and (e) ILPA-compliant fee and expense disclosure.
**15.2 Annual Reports**
The General Partner shall provide to each Limited Partner audited financial statements prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP, audited by Graystone Whitaker LLP (or a successor independent auditor), within **120 days** after the end of each fiscal year (i.e., by April 30 of the following year). Annual reports shall include a letter from the General Partner discussing Fund performance, investment activity, and outlook. The General Partner shall host an annual meeting of Limited Partners. Annual reports shall comply with ILPA reporting standards for fee and expense disclosure.
**15.3 Capital Account Statements**
Capital account statements shall be provided quarterly, within **60 days** after the end of each fiscal quarter. Capital account statements shall include: contributions, distributions, allocations of income/loss, management fee charges, and ending capital account balance.
**15.4 ESG Reporting**
The General Partner shall provide an **annual ESG report** to all Limited Partners within **150 days** after the end of each fiscal year. The ESG report shall include:
> \(a\) A report prepared in accordance with the **UN Principles for Responsible Investment (\"UN PRI\")** framework, including the General Partner\'s PRI assessment report (if applicable);
>
> \(b\) **SFDR disclosures** (Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation) as applicable to Limited Partners subject to SFDR reporting requirements, including principal adverse impact indicators and sustainability risk assessments;
>
> \(c\) **TCFD-aligned climate risk assessments** (Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures), including identification of climate-related risks and opportunities across the portfolio, scenario analysis (where practicable), and metrics and targets for greenhouse gas emissions (Scope 1, 2, and, where available, Scope 3);
>
> \(d\) A summary of ESG integration practices across the investment process, including pre-investment due diligence, active ownership, and monitoring; and
>
> \(e\) Portfolio-level ESG key performance indicators (KPIs) and progress against stated ESG objectives.
The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to adopt and implement ESG policies consistent with leading institutional investor expectations.
**[Section 16: Side Letters and MFN]{.underline}**
**16.1 Side Letters**
The General Partner may enter into side letters or other supplemental agreements with individual Limited Partners granting such Limited Partners rights or accommodations in addition to, or different from, those set forth in the LPA. Side letter accommodations may include, without limitation: (a) MFN election rights, (b) fee discounts or modified fee arrangements, (c) enhanced or additional reporting, (d) transfer rights, (e) co-investment rights, and (f) other accommodations consistent with the terms of the LPA.
**16.2 Most Favored Nation (MFN) Rights**
**MFN Threshold.** Only Limited Partners with capital commitments of **\$75 million or more** shall be entitled to MFN election rights.
**MFN Election Window.** Within **30 days** following the Final Closing, the General Partner shall provide each eligible Limited Partner with a summary of all side letter provisions granted to other Limited Partners. Each eligible Limited Partner shall have 30 days from receipt of such summary to elect to receive the benefit of any such provisions.
**MFN Carve-Outs.** The following categories of side letter provisions shall be **excluded** from MFN elections:
> \(a\) **Tax-related provisions** specific to the requesting Limited Partner\'s tax status or jurisdiction;
>
> \(b\) **Regulatory accommodations** specific to the requesting Limited Partner\'s regulatory requirements or jurisdiction; and
>
> \(c\) **LPAC membership**.
**[Section 17: Transfers]{.underline}**
Interests in the Fund may not be transferred without the prior written consent of the General Partner (which consent may be withheld in the General Partner\'s sole and absolute discretion). Transfers to affiliates of a Limited Partner may be permitted without GP consent, subject to compliance with applicable securities laws and tax requirements. The General Partner may establish secondary transfer programs or facilitate secondary market transactions at its discretion. All transfers are subject to compliance with applicable federal and state securities laws, including restrictions under Regulation D and Rule 144.
**[Section 18: Term and Dissolution]{.underline}**
**Fund Term.** The Fund shall continue in existence for ten (10) years from the date of the Final Closing (expected: April 15, 2026 through April 15, 2036), unless earlier dissolved.
**Extensions.** The General Partner may extend the Fund Term for up to **two (2) successive one (1)-year periods** (to a maximum of April 15, 2038) by providing at least 90 days\' prior written notice to the Limited Partners. (Cross-reference to Section 4.)
**Dissolution Events.** The Fund shall be dissolved upon: (a) expiration of the Fund Term (as extended); (b) removal of the General Partner without appointment of a successor; (c) a vote of 80% in Interest of the Limited Partners; or (d) entry of a decree of judicial dissolution.
**Winding Up.** Upon dissolution, the General Partner (or a liquidating agent appointed by the Limited Partners) shall wind up the affairs of the Fund in an orderly manner, liquidate assets, pay debts and obligations, and distribute remaining assets in accordance with the waterfall.
**[Section 19: Indemnification and Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**
The Fund shall indemnify the General Partner, the Management Company, and their respective members, officers, employees, and agents (each an \"Indemnified Person\") against any losses, claims, damages, liabilities, and expenses arising out of or relating to the Fund\'s activities, except to the extent arising from fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence. The standard of care for the General Partner shall be gross negligence (not mere negligence or a reasonableness standard). The General Partner shall not be liable for any errors of judgment or mistakes of fact or law, provided that the General Partner acted in good faith and in a manner reasonably believed to be in the best interests of the Fund.
**[Section 20: Confidentiality]{.underline}**
All information provided to Limited Partners regarding the Fund\'s activities, portfolio companies, and other Partners shall be treated as confidential. Exceptions: (a) disclosures required by law, regulation, or court order; (b) disclosures to advisors under confidentiality obligations; (c) disclosures to regulatory authorities; and (d) information that becomes publicly available through no fault of the disclosing party.
The General Partner acknowledges that certain Limited Partners (including public pension funds such as Kestrel Institutional Partners) may be subject to freedom of information or public records laws. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with such Limited Partners to preserve confidentiality to the extent permitted by applicable law.
**[Section 21: Miscellaneous]{.underline}**
**Governing Law.** This Term Sheet and the definitive LPA shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflicts of law principles.
**Dispute Resolution.** Disputes shall be resolved through binding arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware, in accordance with the rules of the American Arbitration Association.
**Amendments.** The LPA may be amended with the written consent of the General Partner and Limited Partners holding at least 66⅔% in Interest, provided that no amendment that adversely affects the economic rights of any Limited Partner shall be effective without such Limited Partner\'s consent.
**Notices.** All notices shall be in writing and delivered to the addresses set forth in the LPA or such other address as may be designated in writing.
**Entire Agreement.** The definitive LPA, together with all schedules, exhibits, and side letters, shall constitute the entire agreement among the parties.
**Severability.** If any provision of the LPA is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.
**Counterparts.** The LPA may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

[280|Normal] (d) Hedging Arrangements. The General Partner may enter into hedging arrangements (including interest rate swaps, currency hedges, and other derivative instruments) on behalf of the Partnership for the purpose of managing risk in connection with Portfolio Investments or other obligations of the Partnership.
[281|Normal] (e) Indemnity Bonds. The General Partner may cause the Partnership to post indemnity bonds, letters of credit, or similar instruments in connection with the Partnership's investment activities.
[282|Normal] (f) Subscription Line Facility. The General Partner may cause the Partnership to enter into one or more subscription line credit facilities (each, a "Subscription Facility") secured by the unfunded Capital Commitments of the Limited Partners. Outstanding borrowings under any Subscription Facility shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of unfunded Capital Commitments at any time. Draws on any Subscription Facility may not remain outstanding for more than two hundred seventy (270) days. The General Partner shall report to the Limited Partners on a quarterly basis regarding the outstanding balance and terms of any Subscription Facility. Each Limited Partner, by executing this Agreement, acknowledges and consents to the pledge of its unfunded Capital Commitment as collateral for any Subscription Facility.
[283|Normal] Section 6.6 — Temporary Investments
[284|Normal] Pending investment in Portfolio Companies, the General Partner may invest Partnership funds in cash and cash equivalents, money market accounts, certificates of deposit, United States government or agency securities, repurchase agreements secured by United States government securities, investment-grade commercial paper, and other short-term, liquid, investment-grade instruments. Interest and other income earned on such temporary investments shall be treated as income of the Partnership.
[285|Normal] Section 6.7 — Recycling of Proceeds
[286|Normal] (a) The General Partner may reinvest ("recycle") Disposition proceeds (whether attributable to the return of capital or to profits) received within thirty-six (36) months of the date of the related Portfolio Investment (the amounts so reinvested, "Recycled Amounts"). For purposes of this Section 6.7, the "date of the related Portfolio Investment" means the date on which the Partnership initially funded its investment in the relevant Portfolio Company (or, in the case of a follow-on investment, the date of such follow-on investment).
[287|Normal] (b) The aggregate Recycled Amounts over the life of the Partnership shall not exceed one hundred fifty percent (150%) of Aggregate Commitments. For purposes of this calculation, each dollar of Disposition proceeds that is reinvested pursuant to this Section 6.7 shall be counted once as a Recycled Amount, regardless of the number of times such dollar is subsequently invested and reinvested.
[288|Normal] (c) Recycling of Disposition proceeds shall be permitted during the Investment Period and for a period of one (1) year following the expiration of the Investment Period (i.e., through March 12, 2027). Following such date, no further recycling shall be permitted, and all Disposition proceeds shall be distributed to the Partners in accordance with Article VII.
[289|Normal] (d) To the extent any Recycled Amounts include proceeds attributable to Net Profits, such amounts shall first be distributed through the waterfall set forth in Section 7.2 before being reinvested; provided that amounts attributable solely to the return of capital may be recycled without first being distributed through the waterfall. The General Partner shall determine in good faith the allocation of Disposition proceeds between capital and profits for purposes of this Section 6.7(d).
[290|Normal] (e) Recycled Amounts shall be deemed unfunded Capital Commitments for purposes of future Capital Calls and shall be available for investment in new or follow-on Portfolio Investments. Recycled Amounts shall not be counted as new Capital Contributions for purposes of calculating the Preferred Return under Section 7.2(b) or Section 7.7.
[291|Normal] (f) The General Partner shall include in each quarterly report delivered pursuant to Section 12.1 a summary of all Recycled Amounts during the relevant quarter, specifying the source Portfolio Investment, the amount recycled, and the allocation between capital and profits.
[292|Normal] Section 6.8 — Co-Investment
[293|Normal] (a) The General Partner shall offer co-investment opportunities ("Co-Investment Opportunities") to the Limited Partners (and their Affiliates) before offering such opportunities to any third party.
[294|Normal] (b) The allocation of Co-Investment Opportunities among the Limited Partners shall be determined by the General Partner in its sole discretion, taking into consideration such factors as the General Partner deems relevant, including the size of each Limited Partner's Capital Commitment, the ability of each Limited Partner to move quickly and decisively, and the relationship of each Limited Partner with the Partnership.
[295|Normal] (c) No Management Fee or Carried Interest shall be charged on co-investments made by Limited Partners (or their Affiliates) alongside the Partnership, unless otherwise agreed in a co-investment vehicle Side Letter or the organizational documents of the applicable co-investment vehicle.
[296|Normal] (d) The General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners of each Co-Investment Opportunity within five (5) Business Days of the Fund's commitment to the applicable Portfolio Investment. Such notice shall include a summary of the proposed transaction, the estimated co-investment amount available, and the timeline for investment decisions.
[298|Normal] ARTICLE VII — DISTRIBUTIONS AND WATERFALL
[299|Normal] Section 7.1 — Timing of Distributions
[300|Normal] (a) The General Partner shall distribute Net Proceeds from each Disposition to the Partners as promptly as practicable following the receipt by the Partnership of such Net Proceeds, but in no event later than sixty (60) days following receipt thereof; provided that the General Partner may retain and establish reasonable reserves for contingent liabilities, anticipated expenses, and other obligations of the Partnership.
[301|Normal] (b) Distributions shall be made in cash unless the General Partner determines, with the consent of the Advisory Committee, to make in-kind distributions of securities or other property to the Partners. Any in-kind distribution shall be valued at fair market value as determined by the General Partner in good faith (with reference to the most recent valuation by the Valuation Firm, if applicable). In-kind distributions of Publicly Traded Securities shall be valued based on the volume-weighted average closing price for the ten (10) trading days preceding the Distribution Date.
[302|Normal] (c) Interim distributions may be made from time to time at the discretion of the General Partner, from current income, interest, dividends, or other receipts of the Partnership.
[303|Normal] (d) Each Distribution shall be allocated among the Partners in accordance with Section 7.2 on a deal-by-deal basis as set forth therein. For the avoidance of doubt, the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 7.2 shall be applied separately with respect to the Net Proceeds from each Realized Investment, and not on an aggregate or whole-fund basis (except as provided in Section 13.4 upon final dissolution of the Partnership).
[304|Normal] Section 7.2 — Distribution Waterfall (Deal-by-Deal)
[305|Normal] With respect to each Realized Investment, the Net Proceeds attributable to such Realized Investment (after deducting the allocable share of Partnership Expenses and reserves, and after taking into account any Netting Reserve pursuant to Section 7.4) shall be distributed among the Partners in the following order of priority:
[306|Normal] (a) Return of Capital (Deal-Specific). First, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Capital Contributions attributable to such Realized Investment, until each such Limited Partner has received an amount equal to the aggregate Capital Contributions made by such Limited Partner that are attributable to such Realized Investment (including such Limited Partner's allocable share of Organizational Expenses, Management Fees, and Partnership Expenses funded with Capital Contributions drawn in respect of such Realized Investment).
[307|Normal] (b) Preferred Return (Deal-Specific). Second, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Capital Contributions attributable to such Realized Investment, until each such Limited Partner has received, with respect to such Realized Investment, an amount equal to a cumulative, compounded preferred return of seven percent (7%) per annum, compounded quarterly, on such Limited Partner's Unreturned Capital Contributions attributable to such Realized Investment, calculated from the date each such Capital Contribution was made through the date of the relevant Distribution (the "Preferred Return").
[308|Normal] (c) GP Catch-Up (Deal-Specific). Third, eighty percent (80%) to the General Partner and twenty percent (20%) to the Limited Partners (pro rata in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests), until the General Partner has received an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of the cumulative amounts distributed pursuant to clauses (b) and (c) of this Section 7.2 with respect to such Realized Investment (the "GP Catch-Up Amount"). For the avoidance of doubt, the GP Catch-Up is intended to result in the General Partner receiving, in the aggregate, twenty percent (20%) of all amounts distributed in excess of the return of capital to the Limited Partners under clause (a) with respect to such Realized Investment, once the GP Catch-Up has been fully satisfied.
[309|Normal] (d) Carried Interest Split (Deal-Specific). Thereafter, eighty percent (80%) to the Limited Partners (pro rata in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests) and twenty percent (20%) to the General Partner.
[310|Normal] For purposes of determining the General Partner's entitlement to Carried Interest under this Section 7.2, see also Section 7.4 (Netting Reserve) and Section 7.5 (Interim Clawback). The General Partner's share of distributions under Sections 7.2(c) and 7.2(d) constitutes the "Carried Interest" payable to the General Partner hereunder.
[311|Normal] Section 7.3 — Escrow of Carried Interest Distributions
[312|Normal] (a) Notwithstanding Sections 7.2(c) and 7.2(d), twenty-five percent (25%) of all Carried Interest distributions otherwise payable to the General Partner pursuant to Sections 7.2(c) and 7.2(d) shall not be distributed to the General Partner but shall instead be deposited into the Carried Interest Escrow account maintained by the Escrow Agent (Northbrook Trust Company) pursuant to the Escrow Agreement. The remaining seventy-five percent (75%) of such Carried Interest distributions shall be distributed to the General Partner in accordance with Section 7.2.
[313|Normal] (b) Amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow shall be released to the General Partner upon the earliest of: (i) the final liquidation and dissolution of the Partnership, subject to the Clawback obligation set forth in Section 7.6 (and after giving effect to any amounts required to satisfy such Clawback obligation); or (ii) at such earlier time as the General Partner determines in good faith, and the Advisory Committee consents (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld), that no Clawback obligation exists or is reasonably likely to arise based on the current portfolio valuations, the aggregate distributions to date, and the remaining Portfolio Investments of the Partnership.
[314|Normal] (c) Amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow shall be invested in money market instruments, United States Treasury securities, or other cash equivalents, as directed by the General Partner.
[315|Normal] (d) Interest and other income earned on amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow shall be credited to the General Partner's account within the escrow but shall remain in the Carried Interest Escrow until such amounts are released to the General Partner pursuant to Section 7.3(b) or applied to satisfy the Clawback obligation pursuant to Section 7.6.
[316|Normal] (e) A summary of the terms of the Escrow Agreement is set forth in Exhibit C.
[317|Normal] Section 7.4 — Netting Reserve
[318|Normal] (a) Prior to distributing any Carried Interest to the General Partner with respect to any Realized Investment pursuant to Sections 7.2(c) and 7.2(d), the General Partner shall calculate the aggregate net unrealized losses (if any) on all other Portfolio Investments then held by the Partnership (the "Netting Reserve"). For purposes of this Section 7.4, "net unrealized losses" means the amount, if any, by which the aggregate unrealized losses on all remaining Portfolio Investments (determined based on the most recent quarterly valuation prepared in accordance with Section 12.6) exceed the aggregate unrealized gains on all remaining Portfolio Investments.
[319|Normal] (b) If the aggregate unrealized losses exceed the aggregate unrealized gains across the remaining portfolio (as determined by the General Partner in good faith, based on the most recent quarterly valuation prepared in accordance with Section 12.6), the General Partner shall withhold from Carried Interest distributions otherwise payable to the General Partner with respect to such Realized Investment an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of such net unrealized losses (the "Netting Reserve Amount").
[320|Normal] (c) Netting Reserve Amounts withheld pursuant to this Section 7.4 shall be deposited in the Carried Interest Escrow and shall be subject to re-evaluation at each subsequent Distribution Date. If, at any subsequent Distribution Date, the aggregate net unrealized losses have decreased (whether by reason of subsequent Dispositions at a gain, increases in the valuation of remaining Portfolio Investments, or otherwise), the General Partner shall release from the Carried Interest Escrow to the General Partner an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of such decrease, subject to the overall limitations of the Clawback obligation set forth in Section 7.6.
[321|Normal] (d) The Advisory Committee may, at any time, request that the Valuation Firm (Ridgepoint Valuations Inc.) provide an independent assessment of unrealized gains and losses for purposes of the Netting Reserve calculation under this Section 7.4. The fees and expenses of the Valuation Firm in connection with any such assessment shall be borne by the Partnership as a Partnership Expense.
[322|Normal] (e) The Netting Reserve adjustments shall be reflected in the Capital Accounts of the Partners in accordance with Section 8.3.
[323|Normal] Section 7.5 — Interim Clawback
[324|Normal] (a) In addition to the final Clawback obligation set forth in Section 7.6, if, at any time after the General Partner has received Carried Interest distributions with respect to one or more Realized Investments, subsequent Dispositions result in aggregate losses to the Limited Partners such that the General Partner has, on a cumulative basis across all Realized Investments to date, received Carried Interest distributions in excess of twenty percent (20%) of cumulative Net Profits (calculated across all Realized Investments to date, after deducting all allocable Partnership Expenses and reserves), the General Partner shall, within ninety (90) days of the relevant Distribution Date, return to the Partnership the amount of such excess (the "Interim Clawback Amount").
[325|Normal] (b) The Interim Clawback Amount shall be calculated on a pre-tax basis. For the avoidance of doubt, unlike the final Clawback obligation set forth in Section 7.6(b), no adjustment shall be made for taxes paid or payable by the General Partner or its members on prior Carried Interest distributions.
[326|Normal] (c) The General Partner may satisfy its Interim Clawback obligation, in whole or in part, from amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow. To the extent that amounts in the Carried Interest Escrow are insufficient to satisfy the Interim Clawback Amount, the General Partner shall fund the balance from its own resources within sixty (60) days following the expiration of the ninety (90)-day period specified in clause (a) above.
[327|Normal] (d) The General Partner shall provide the Advisory Committee with a written calculation of the Interim Clawback Amount and supporting documentation (including a schedule of all Carried Interest distributions received to date, a schedule of all Realized Investments and the Net Profits or Net Losses attributable thereto, and a calculation of cumulative Net Profits) within thirty (30) days of each Distribution Date. The Advisory Committee shall have the right to review such calculation and to request additional information or independent verification by the Accounting Firm.
[328|Normal] Section 7.6 — Clawback Obligation (Final)
[329|Normal] (a) Upon the final liquidation and dissolution of the Partnership, the General Partner shall determine whether it has received aggregate Carried Interest distributions (including amounts released from the Carried Interest Escrow) in excess of twenty percent (20%) of the cumulative Net Profits of the Partnership (after giving effect to: (i) the return of all Capital Contributions to the Limited Partners; and (ii) the payment of the Preferred Return thereon at a rate of seven percent (7%) per annum, compounded quarterly, calculated from the date of each Capital Contribution through the date of the relevant Distribution or the date of final dissolution, as applicable). If the General Partner has received Carried Interest distributions in excess of such amount, the General Partner shall return such excess (the "Clawback Amount") to the Partnership for distribution to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests.
[330|Normal] (b) The Clawback obligation under this Section 7.6 shall be calculated on an after-tax basis, assuming a combined federal, state, and local income tax rate of forty percent (40%) applied to the Carried Interest distributions previously received by the General Partner. The General Partner shall provide the Advisory Committee and the Limited Partners with a detailed written calculation of the Clawback Amount, including the after-tax adjustment, within sixty (60) days following the final dissolution of the Partnership.
[331|Normal] (c) The General Partner shall be personally obligated to fund the Clawback Amount; provided, however, that amounts then held in the Carried Interest Escrow shall first be applied to satisfy such obligation. To the extent that amounts in the Carried Interest Escrow are insufficient to satisfy the Clawback Amount, the General Partner (and, to the extent applicable, the individual members of the General Partner receiving Carried Interest distributions) shall fund the balance from their own resources within ninety (90) days following the final dissolution of the Partnership.
[332|Normal] (d) The Clawback obligation under this Section 7.6 shall survive the dissolution and termination of the Partnership for a period of three (3) years. The General Partner's obligation to fund the Clawback Amount shall be an unconditional obligation, enforceable against the General Partner (and its successors and assigns) by any Limited Partner or group of Limited Partners.
[333|Normal] (e) Amounts returned by the General Partner pursuant to Section 7.5 (Interim Clawback) shall be credited against the Clawback obligation under this Section 7.6. For the avoidance of doubt, the General Partner shall not be required to return amounts under both Section 7.5 and this Section 7.6 with respect to the same excess Carried Interest.
[334|Normal] Section 7.7 — Distribution Reinvestment; Preferred Return on Reinvested Amounts
[335|Normal] (a) If the General Partner determines to recycle Disposition proceeds pursuant to Section 6.7, such amounts shall not be distributed through the waterfall set forth in Section 7.2 (except to the extent required by Section 6.7(d) with respect to the profit component of such proceeds) but shall instead be retained by the Partnership and treated as available for reinvestment in new or follow-on Portfolio Investments.
[336|Normal] (b) For purposes of calculating the Preferred Return under Section 7.2(b), reinvested amounts (Recycled Amounts) shall be treated as if such amounts had been returned to the Limited Partners and immediately re-contributed to the Partnership by such Limited Partners; provided that the Preferred Return shall continue to accrue on the original Capital Contribution at a rate of seven percent (7%) per annum, compounded quarterly, until such Capital Contribution is fully returned to the relevant Limited Partner through actual cash Distributions. Recycled Amounts shall not be counted as new Capital Contributions for purposes of calculating the Preferred Return.
[337|Normal] (c) The General Partner shall maintain detailed records of all Recycled Amounts and shall provide the Limited Partners with a reconciliation of Recycled Amounts in connection with each quarterly report delivered pursuant to Section 12.1.
[338|Normal] Section 7.8 — Withholding
[339|Normal] (a) The General Partner is authorized and directed to withhold from any Distribution to any Partner any amounts required to be withheld under the Code, Treasury Regulations, or any provision of any state, local, or foreign tax law. Any amounts so withheld shall be treated as having been distributed to the affected Partner for all purposes of this Agreement, including for purposes of the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 7.2 and for purposes of maintaining such Partner's Capital Account under Section 8.1.
[340|Normal] (b) Each Partner shall provide the General Partner with such tax forms, certifications, and other information as the General Partner may reasonably request in order to determine whether any withholding is required with respect to Distributions to such Partner.
[341|Normal] (c) If the Partnership incurs a withholding tax obligation with respect to any Partner's share of Partnership income (other than in connection with a Distribution), the amount of such withholding tax shall be treated as a Distribution to such Partner and shall reduce subsequent Distributions to such Partner accordingly.
[342|Normal] Section 7.9 — Tax Distributions
[343|Normal] (a) The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make quarterly tax distributions ("Tax Distributions") to the Partners in an amount estimated by the General Partner, in consultation with the Accounting Firm, to be sufficient to enable each Partner to satisfy its United States federal and state income tax liabilities attributable to such Partner's allocable share of the Partnership's taxable income for the relevant period. Tax Distributions shall be calculated based on the highest combined marginal rate of United States federal and applicable state income tax applicable to individuals or corporations (whichever is higher) resident in New York, New York.
[344|Normal] (b) Tax Distributions shall be treated as advances against, and shall reduce, future Distributions to which such Partner would otherwise be entitled under the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 7.2.
[345|Normal] (c) The General Partner shall not be required to make Tax Distributions to the extent that such Distributions would impair the Partnership's ability to fund its operations, make Portfolio Investments, or satisfy its outstanding obligations.
[346|Normal] (d) The General Partner shall provide each Partner with an estimate of such Partner's taxable income for each Fiscal Year within ninety (90) days after the end of such Fiscal Year, together with such Partner's Schedule K-1 (or a preliminary estimate thereof).
[348|Normal] ARTICLE VIII — ALLOCATIONS
[349|Normal] Section 8.1 — Capital Accounts
[350|Normal] (a) A separate Capital Account shall be established and maintained for each Partner in accordance with the rules of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv). Each Partner's Capital Account shall be:
[351|Normal] (i) credited with: (A) the amount of cash contributed by such Partner to the Partnership; (B) the agreed fair market value of any property (other than cash) contributed by such Partner to the Partnership (net of any liabilities secured by such property that the Partnership is considered to assume or take subject to under Section 752 of the Code); and (C) such Partner's allocable share of Net Profits and items of income and gain allocated to such Partner pursuant to this Article VIII;
[352|Normal] (ii) debited with: (A) the amount of cash distributed to such Partner by the Partnership; (B) the agreed fair market value of any property (other than cash) distributed to such Partner by the Partnership (net of any liabilities secured by such property that such Partner is considered to assume or take subject to under Section 752 of the Code); and (C) such Partner's allocable share of Net Losses and items of loss and deduction allocated to such Partner pursuant to this Article VIII.
[353|Normal] (b) The Capital Account of any transferee of all or a portion of a Partner's Interest shall be determined in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(l).
[354|Normal] (c) The General Partner may, in its discretion, adjust the Capital Accounts

[355|Normal] Section 8.2 — Allocations of Net Profits and Net Losses
[356|Normal] (a) Net Profits. Net Profits for each Fiscal Year (or other relevant period) shall be allocated among the Partners in a manner consistent with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 7.2, such that, to the greatest extent possible, the Capital Account balances of the Partners reflect the amounts that would be distributed to each Partner if the Partnership were dissolved, its assets sold at their Gross Asset Value, and the net proceeds distributed in accordance with Section 7.2.
[357|Normal] (b) Net Losses. Net Losses for each Fiscal Year (or other relevant period) shall be allocated among the Partners in a manner consistent with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 7.2, in reverse order of priority; provided that Net Losses shall not be allocated to any Partner to the extent that such allocation would cause such Partner to have an Adjusted Capital Account deficit at the end of the relevant Fiscal Year.
[358|Normal] (c) Regulatory Allocations. The following special allocations shall be made in the following order of priority, before any other allocations under this Article VIII:
[359|Normal] (i) Qualified Income Offset. If any Partner unexpectedly receives any adjustment, allocation, or distribution described in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), or (6) that causes or increases an Adjusted Capital Account deficit for such Partner, items of Partnership income and gain shall be specially allocated to such Partner in an amount and manner sufficient to eliminate such Adjusted Capital Account deficit as quickly as possible.
[360|Normal] (ii) Gross Income Allocation. If any Partner has an Adjusted Capital Account deficit at the end of any Fiscal Year, items of Partnership gross income and gain shall be allocated to such Partner in an amount and manner sufficient to eliminate such deficit as quickly as possible.
[361|Normal] (iii) Minimum Gain Chargeback. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article VIII, if there is a net decrease in Partnership minimum gain during any Fiscal Year, each Partner shall be allocated items of Partnership income and gain for such Fiscal Year (and, if necessary, subsequent Fiscal Years) in an amount and manner consistent with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(f).
[362|Normal] (iv) Partner Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain Chargeback. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article VIII (other than clause (iii) above), if there is a net decrease in partner nonrecourse debt minimum gain attributable to a partner nonrecourse debt during any Fiscal Year, each Partner who has a share of the partner nonrecourse debt minimum gain attributable to such partner nonrecourse debt shall be allocated items of Partnership income and gain for such Fiscal Year (and, if necessary, subsequent Fiscal Years) in an amount and manner consistent with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(i)(4).
[363|Normal] (v) Nonrecourse Deductions. Nonrecourse deductions for any Fiscal Year shall be allocated among the Partners in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests.
[364|Normal] (d) To the extent that any regulatory allocation made pursuant to Section 8.2(c) is inconsistent with the economic arrangement of the Partners as reflected in the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 7.2, subsequent allocations of Net Profits, Net Losses, and other items shall be made so as to offset, to the greatest extent possible, the effect of such regulatory allocation.
[365|Normal] Section 8.3 — Special Allocations; Preferred Return Allocation
[366|Normal] (a) Net Profits shall first be allocated to the Limited Partners to the extent of the Preferred Return (seven percent (7%) per annum, compounded quarterly, on each Limited Partner's Unreturned Capital Contributions), such that each Limited Partner's Capital Account reflects the accrued Preferred Return with respect to such Limited Partner's share of each Realized Investment.
[367|Normal] (b) Thereafter, Net Profits shall be allocated eighty percent (80%) to the Limited Partners (pro rata in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests) and twenty percent (20%) to the General Partner, consistent with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 7.2.
[368|Normal] (c) The General Partner shall make such curative allocations of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit as are necessary to ensure that the allocations under this Article VIII are consistent with the economic arrangement of the Partners as reflected in the distribution waterfall of Section 7.2.
[369|Normal] (d) Allocations under Section 704(c) of the Code with respect to contributed property or revalued property shall be made using the traditional method under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3(b), unless the General Partner determines in its discretion that another reasonable method under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3 is more appropriate.
[370|Normal] Section 8.4 — Tax Allocations
[371|Normal] (a) Except as otherwise provided in this Section 8.4, items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit shall be allocated among the Partners for federal, state, and local income tax purposes in the same manner as the corresponding items are allocated among the Partners pursuant to Sections 8.2 and 8.3.
[372|Normal] (b) In accordance with Section 704(c) of the Code and the Treasury Regulations thereunder, income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to any property contributed to the Partnership shall, solely for tax purposes, be allocated among the Partners so as to take account of any variation between the adjusted basis of such property to the Partnership for federal income tax purposes and its initial Gross Asset Value. Any elections or other decisions relating to such allocations shall be made in a manner that reasonably reflects the purpose and intent of this Agreement.
[373|Normal] (c) The Partnership shall make an election under Section 754 of the Code upon the written request of any transferee of an Interest, at such transferee's expense. The General Partner may, in its discretion, make a Section 754 election at any other time.
[374|Normal] (d) The General Partner shall prepare, or cause the Accounting Firm to prepare, all federal, state, and local income tax returns of the Partnership and shall deliver to each Partner a Schedule K-1 (or equivalent form) on or before the date required for the filing of the Partnership's income tax return for the relevant Fiscal Year (including extensions).
[375|Normal] Section 8.5 — Determinations by General Partner
[376|Normal] All accounting determinations, allocations, and valuations required to be made under this Article VIII (and under Article VII) shall be made by the General Partner in good faith, in consultation with the Accounting Firm (Graystone Whitaker LLP), and shall be final and binding on all Partners, absent manifest error or fraud.
[378|Normal] ARTICLE IX — KEY PERSON
[379|Normal] Section 9.1 — Key Person Event
[380|Normal] (a) The "Key Person" for purposes of this Agreement shall be Richard Holloway.
[381|Normal] (b) A "Key Person Event" shall occur if Richard Holloway ceases to devote substantially all of his business time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership and the Management Company. For purposes of this Section 9.1, the term "substantially all" shall be determined by the General Partner in its reasonable judgment, taking into account all relevant facts and circumstances; provided that a Key Person Event shall not be deemed to have occurred solely by reason of:
[382|Normal] (i) a temporary absence due to illness, injury, or disability for a period not exceeding one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days;
[383|Normal] (ii) reasonable vacation time consistent with the Key Person's past practice; or
[384|Normal] (iii) service on up to three (3) outside boards of directors of entities that do not compete, directly or indirectly, with the Partnership's investment program.
[385|Normal] (c) For the avoidance of doubt, a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred upon the death, permanent disability, or voluntary resignation of Richard Holloway from his position with the Management Company.
[386|Normal] Section 9.2 — Consequences of a Key Person Event
[387|Normal] (a) Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the Investment Period shall be automatically suspended as of the date of such Key Person Event.
[388|Normal] (b) During any suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner shall not make any new Portfolio Investments on behalf of the Partnership; provided that the General Partner may (i) fund investments pursuant to binding commitments entered into prior to the date of the Key Person Event, (ii) make follow-on investments in existing Portfolio Companies that the General Partner determines in good faith are necessary to protect or preserve the value of existing Portfolio Investments, and (iii) continue to pay Management Fees, Partnership Expenses, and other obligations of the Partnership from available funds or unfunded Capital Commitments.
[389|Normal] (c) The Investment Period may be reinstated by the affirmative vote (or written consent) of a majority in Interest (more than fifty percent (50%)) of all Limited Partners (not merely those present or voting at a meeting). If the Limited Partners vote to reinstate the Investment Period, such reinstatement shall be effective as of the date of such vote and the General Partner shall resume making new Portfolio Investments in accordance with this Agreement.
[390|Normal] (d) If the Investment Period is not reinstated within twelve (12) months of the date of the Key Person Event, the Investment Period shall be permanently terminated, and the General Partner shall commence an orderly wind-down of the Partnership's investment program. During such wind-down period, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to liquidate or distribute the remaining Portfolio Investments in an orderly manner, consistent with maximizing value for the Limited Partners.
[391|Normal] Section 9.3 — Notification
[392|Normal] The General Partner shall provide written notice to all Limited Partners and the members of the Advisory Committee within five (5) Business Days of the occurrence or reasonably anticipated occurrence of a Key Person Event. Such notice shall describe the circumstances giving rise to the Key Person Event and the General Partner's assessment of the impact on the Partnership's investment program.
[394|Normal] ARTICLE X — REMOVAL OF GENERAL PARTNER
[395|Normal] Section 10.1 — Removal for Cause
[396|Normal] (a) For purposes of this Agreement, "Cause" means: (i) fraud; (ii) willful misconduct; (iii) gross negligence; or (iv) conviction of (or entry of a plea of guilty or nolo contendere to) a felony, in each case by the General Partner or any Key Person, as determined by a final, non-appealable judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction.
[397|Normal] (b) The General Partner may be removed for Cause by the affirmative vote (or written consent) of Limited Partners holding at least fifty percent (50%) in Interest of all Limited Partners (not merely those present or voting at a meeting).
[398|Normal] (c) Upon removal for Cause, the General Partner shall forfeit all rights to Carried Interest, both realized (to the extent not yet distributed from the Carried Interest Escrow or otherwise) and unrealized, as of the date of removal. Any amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow at the time of removal for Cause shall be distributed to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests. The General Partner shall not be entitled to any further Management Fees from and after the date of removal for Cause.
[399|Normal] (d) Following the removal of the General Partner for Cause, a successor General Partner may be elected by the affirmative vote (or written consent) of a majority in Interest of all Limited Partners. The successor General Partner shall assume all rights and obligations of the removed General Partner under this Agreement, except for the Clawback obligation under Section 7.6 and the indemnification obligations under Section 17.10, which shall remain the personal obligations of the removed General Partner.
[400|Normal] Section 10.2 — No-Fault Removal
[401|Normal] (a) The General Partner may be removed without Cause by the affirmative vote (or written consent) of Limited Partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) in Interest of all Limited Partners (not merely those present or voting at a meeting).
[402|Normal] (b) Upon removal without Cause, the General Partner shall be entitled to receive Carried Interest distributions with respect to Portfolio Investments that have been realized (i.e., disposed of) prior to the effective date of removal, calculated in accordance with the waterfall set forth in Section 7.2 as if the Partnership were dissolved on such date, but only with respect to actual Disposition proceeds received by the Partnership prior to such date (and not with respect to any unrealized appreciation, fair market value, or hypothetical liquidation value of unsold Portfolio Investments). For the avoidance of doubt, the General Partner's entitlement to Carried Interest upon removal without Cause is limited to amounts attributable to actual cash (or cash-equivalent) Disposition proceeds received by the Partnership, and shall not include any amounts attributable to the estimated or appraised value of Portfolio Investments that remain unsold as of the effective date of removal.
[403|Normal] (c) Upon removal without Cause, the General Partner shall have no further entitlement to Carried Interest with respect to Portfolio Investments that are realized after the effective date of removal, and all such Carried Interest shall instead be allocated to the successor General Partner (if any) or distributed to the Limited Partners in accordance with the waterfall set forth in Section 7.2 (with the Carried Interest portion allocated to the Limited Partners, pro rata).
[404|Normal] (d) Management Fees shall cease as of the effective date of removal without Cause, and the General Partner shall not be entitled to any further Management Fees from and after such date.
[405|Normal] (e) Following the removal of the General Partner without Cause, a successor General Partner may be elected by the affirmative vote (or written consent) of a majority in Interest of all Limited Partners. The successor General Partner shall assume all rights and obligations of the removed General Partner under this Agreement, subject to the limitations set forth in this Section 10.2.
[406|Normal] (f) The removed General Partner shall cooperate fully in an orderly transition of the management and affairs of the Partnership to the successor General Partner, including the transfer of all books, records, files, and documents relating to the Partnership's affairs. The removed General Partner shall not be released from its Clawback obligations under Section 7.6 or any indemnification obligations under Section 17.10 as a result of its removal. For purposes of the Fund Term provisions of Section 13.1 (including any extensions thereof), the removal of the General Partner without Cause shall not, by itself, cause a dissolution of the Partnership or a termination of the Fund Term.
[407|Normal] Section 10.3 — Voting Procedures for Removal
[408|Normal] (a) Any vote to remove the General Partner pursuant to Section 10.1 or Section 10.2 shall be conducted by written ballot circulated to all Limited Partners. The General Partner shall, within five (5) Business Days of receiving a written request from Limited Partners holding at least twenty-five percent (25%) in Interest of all Limited Partners, circulate a ballot to all Limited Partners requesting a vote on the removal of the General Partner.
[409|Normal] (b) The ballot shall specify the grounds for removal (Cause or no-fault) and the applicable voting threshold. Each Limited Partner shall have sixty (60) days from the date of the ballot to submit its vote. Votes may be submitted by hand delivery, overnight courier, or email to the address specified in the ballot.
[410|Normal] (c) The General Partner shall be entitled to present its position to the Limited Partners in writing within thirty (30) days of the date of the ballot, and such written response shall be circulated to all Limited Partners.
[411|Normal] (d) The Limited Partners may retain independent legal counsel at the Partnership's expense to advise them in connection with any proposed removal vote.
[412|Normal] (e) The results of the removal vote shall be tabulated by the Fund Administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC) and communicated to all Partners within five (5) Business Days following the expiration of the sixty (60)-day voting period.
[414|Normal] ARTICLE XI — LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE
[415|Normal] Section 11.1 — Establishment and Composition
[416|Normal] (a) The General Partner shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the "Advisory Committee" or "LPAC") consisting of not fewer than three (3) and not more than five (5) members, each of whom shall be a representative designated by a Limited Partner.
[417|Normal] (b) Members of the Advisory Committee shall be appointed by the General Partner, in consultation with the Limited Partners. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the Advisory Committee includes representatives of Limited Partners with diverse perspectives, including public pension funds, corporate pension plans, endowments, foundations, and other institutional investors.
[418|Normal] (c) Each member of the Advisory Committee shall serve until the earlier of: (i) the dissolution of the Partnership; (ii) the withdrawal, removal, or transfer of the entire Interest of the appointing Limited Partner; or (iii) replacement by the General Partner with the consent of a majority of the then-serving members of the Advisory Committee.
[419|Normal] (d) The Advisory Committee is an advisory body only. The Advisory Committee's consent (or refusal to consent) with respect to any matter shall not create any fiduciary duty owed by the members of the Advisory Committee to any Partner or to the Partnership. No member of the Advisory Committee shall have any personal liability to the Partnership or to any Partner by reason of its service on the Advisory Committee, except as provided in Section 11.5.
[420|Normal] Section 11.2 — Meetings and Quorum
[421|Normal] (a) The Advisory Committee shall meet not less frequently than semi-annually, at such times and places (including the principal office of the Partnership or such other location) as determined by the General Partner.
[422|Normal] (b) The General Partner shall provide not less than ten (10) Business Days' advance written notice of each meeting of the Advisory Committee, together with a proposed agenda and any materials to be discussed at such meeting. Notice may be given by email to the addresses provided by the Advisory Committee members.
[423|Normal] (c) Special meetings of the Advisory Committee may be called by the General Partner or by any two (2) members of the Advisory Committee upon not less than five (5) Business Days' advance written notice to all members and the General Partner.
[424|Normal] (d) A majority of the members of the Advisory Committee shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting. Actions of the Advisory Committee shall be taken by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present at a meeting at which a quorum is present.
[425|Normal] (e) Meetings of the Advisory Committee may be held in person, by teleconference, or by videoconference, as determined by the General Partner or, in the case of special meetings, by the members calling such meeting. The Advisory Committee may also act by written consent in lieu of a meeting, signed by a majority of the members.
[426|Normal] Section 11.3 — Consent Rights
[427|Normal] The General Partner shall seek the prior consent (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed) of the Advisory Committee with respect to the following matters:
[428|Normal] (a) Conflicts of Interest. Any transaction between the Partnership, on the one hand, and the General Partner, the Management Company, or any of their respective Affiliates, on the other hand (other than the payment of Management Fees pursuant to Section 5.1 and Co-Investment arrangements that are offered to all Limited Partners in accordance with Section 6.8), including any transaction in which the General Partner or its Affiliates have a material financial interest that is adverse to the interest of the Partnership.
[429|Normal] (b) Extension of Fund Term. Any extension of the Fund Term pursuant to Section 13.1(b), including the duration and terms of any such extension.
[430|Normal] (c) Modification of Fee Terms. Any amendment to the Management Fee provisions of Section 5.1, any modification of the fee offset provisions of Section 5.1(d), or any other change to the economic terms of the General Partner's or the Management Company's compensation.
[431|Normal] (d) Release of Carried Interest Escrow. Any release of amounts from the Carried Interest Escrow prior to the final dissolution of the Partnership, as set forth in Section 7.3(b)(ii).
[432|Normal] The Advisory Committee shall act in good faith and with due regard for the interests of all Limited Partners (and not solely the interests of the appointing Limited Partners) in exercising its consent rights under this Section 11.3.
[433|Normal] Section 11.4 — Expenses
[434|Normal] Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred by members of the Advisory Committee in connection with their attendance at meetings of the Advisory Committee (including travel, lodging, and meal expenses) shall be borne by the Partnership as a Partnership Expense.
[435|Normal] Section 11.5 — Indemnification
[436|Normal] The Partnership shall indemnify each member of the Advisory Committee against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses) arising from or in connection with such member's service on the Advisory Committee, to the same extent and subject to the same exceptions as set forth in Section 17.10 with respect to Indemnified Persons; provided that no member shall be indemnified for any losses arising from such member's fraud, gross negligence, or willful misconduct.
[438|Normal] ARTICLE XII — REPORTING AND ACCOUNTING
[439|Normal] Section 12.1 — Quarterly Reports
[440|Normal] Within sixty (60) days after the end of each fiscal quarter, the General Partner shall furnish to each Limited Partner a report containing the following:
[441|Normal] (a) unaudited financial statements of the Partnership for such fiscal quarter, including a balance sheet, a statement of operations, and a statement of changes in partners' capital, prepared in accordance with GAAP;
[442|Normal] (b) a portfolio summary, including an investment-by-investment listing of all Portfolio Investments held by the Partnership as of the end of such fiscal quarter, showing cost, fair market value, and key performance metrics (including gross and net internal rate of return and gross and net multiple of invested capital) for each Portfolio Investment;
[443|Normal] (c) a summary of all Capital Calls made during such fiscal quarter, all Distributions made during such fiscal quarter, and each Limited Partner's unfunded Capital Commitment as of the end of such fiscal quarter;
[444|Normal] (d) a summary of all Recycled Amounts during such fiscal quarter, as required by Section 6.7(f);
[445|Normal] (e) a summary of any outstanding borrowings under any Subscription Facility, as required by Section 6.5(f); and
[446|Normal] (f) a discussion of material developments affecting the Partnership or any Portfolio Company during such fiscal quarter, including any material changes to the General Partner's outlook for the portfolio.
[447|Normal] Section 12.2 — Annual Reports
[448|Normal] Within ninety (90) days after the end of each Fiscal Year, the General Partner shall furnish to each Limited Partner a report containing the following:
[449|Normal] (a) audited financial statements of the Partnership for such Fiscal Year, including a balance sheet, a statement of operations, a statement of changes in partners' capital, and a statement of cash flows, prepared in accordance with GAAP and audited by the Accounting Firm (Graystone Whitaker LLP);
[450|Normal] (b) a Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) for each Partner, reflecting such Partner's allocable share of the Partnership's income, gain, loss, deduction, and credits for such Fiscal Year;
[451|Normal] (c) a report on the operations of the Partnership during such Fiscal Year, including a discussion of Portfolio Investments made and disposed of, material developments at Portfolio Companies, and the General Partner's assessment of the Partnership's overall performance and outlook;
[452|Normal] (d) a schedule of all fees and expenses borne by the Partnership during such Fiscal Year, including Management Fees paid, Partnership Expenses, and the status of the Organizational Expense Cap;
[453|Normal] (e) a schedule of all Carried Interest distributions made to the General Partner during such Fiscal Year, including the status of the Carried Interest Escrow and any Interim Clawback or final Clawback amounts; and
[454|Normal] (f) any other information reasonably requested by any Limited Partner, to the extent such information is available and the General Partner determines in good faith that providing such information would not be unduly burdensome or harmful to the Partnership.
[455|Normal] Section 12.3 — Capital Account Statements
[456|Normal] Within sixty (60) days after the end of each fiscal quarter, the General Partner shall furnish to each Limited Partner a statement showing: (a) such Limited Partner's aggregate Capital Contributions as of the end of such quarter; (b) aggregate Distributions received by such Limited Partner as of the end of such quarter; (c) such Limited Partner's Capital Account balance as of the end of such quarter; and (d) such Limited Partner's unfunded Capital Commitment as of the end of such quarter.
[457|Normal] Section 12.4 — Annual Meeting
[458|Normal] The General Partner shall hold an annual meeting of the Limited Partners within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each Fiscal Year, at a time and place determined by the General Partner (which may include a virtual meeting by videoconference). The purpose of the annual meeting shall be to discuss the Partnership's activities, investment performance, market outlook, and such other matters as the General Partner or the Limited Partners may wish to address. The General Partner shall provide reasonable advance notice of the annual meeting and distribute relevant materials in advance thereof.
[459|Normal] Section 12.5 — Books and Records; Inspection
[460|Normal] (a) The General Partner shall maintain, or cause to be maintained, complete and accurate books and records of the Partnership at the principal office of the Partnership. The Fund Administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC) shall maintain the Partnership's books and records on a day-to-day basis, under the supervision of the General Partner.
[461|Normal] (b) Each Limited Partner (and its designated representatives) shall have the right, at reasonable times an
