Such inspection rights shall be subject to compliance with the confidentiality provisions of Section 12.7.
[462|Normal] Section 12.6 — Valuation
[463|Normal] (a) Portfolio Investments shall be valued at fair market value as determined by the General Partner in good faith, in accordance with GAAP and consistent with the IPEV Guidelines (International Private Equity and Venture Capital Valuation Guidelines).
[464|Normal] (b) The General Partner shall cause the Valuation Firm (Ridgepoint Valuations Inc.) to perform an independent valuation of all Portfolio Investments at least annually, as of the end of each Fiscal Year. The Valuation Firm may also be engaged to perform interim valuations at the request of the General Partner or the Advisory Committee.
[465|Normal] (c) Publicly Traded Securities held by the Partnership shall be valued based on the closing market price as of the applicable valuation date (or, if such date is not a trading day, the most recent prior trading day).
[466|Normal] (d) The General Partner shall report the fair market value of each Portfolio Investment in each quarterly report and annual report delivered to the Limited Partners pursuant to Sections 12.1 and 12.2.
[467|Normal] Section 12.7 — Confidentiality
[468|Normal] (a) All information provided to the Limited Partners and the Advisory Committee in connection with the Partnership's activities (including financial statements, portfolio information, and any other non-public information) shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed by any Limited Partner to any third party without the prior written consent of the General Partner.
[469|Normal] (b) The foregoing confidentiality restriction shall not apply to disclosures: (i) required by applicable law, regulation, or judicial or administrative process (including disclosures required by the Freedom of Information Act or analogous state laws applicable to governmental pension plans); (ii) to a Limited Partner's legal, tax, financial, or other professional advisors who are bound by obligations of confidentiality; (iii) to a Limited Partner's Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents who have a need to know and are bound by obligations of confidentiality; or (iv) to a prospective transferee of a Limited Partner's Interest in connection with a proposed Transfer, subject to the execution of a confidentiality agreement reasonably acceptable to the General Partner.
[470|Normal] (c) Each Limited Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with the General Partner in seeking confidential treatment or protective orders with respect to any information required to be disclosed pursuant to clause (b)(i) above.
[472|Normal] ARTICLE XIII — TERM AND DISSOLUTION
[473|Normal] Section 13.1 — Term of the Partnership
[474|Normal] (a) The Partnership shall continue until the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Final Closing (i.e., March 12, 2031) (the "Scheduled Termination Date"), unless earlier dissolved pursuant to this Article XIII.
[475|Normal] (b) The General Partner may extend the term of the Partnership for one (1) additional period of one (1) year (i.e., through March 12, 2032, at the latest), upon written notice to the Limited Partners and the Advisory Committee delivered not less than ninety (90) days prior to the Scheduled Termination Date (or, if applicable, the then-current expiration date of the Fund Term), provided that the Advisory Committee has consented to such extension pursuant to Section 11.3(b). For the avoidance of doubt, the Fund Term may be extended only once, for a single additional period of one (1) year.
[476|Normal] (c) During any extension period, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to liquidate or distribute the remaining Portfolio Investments in an orderly manner, consistent with maximizing value for the Partners.
[477|Normal] (d) The period from the Effective Date through the Scheduled Termination Date (as the same may be extended pursuant to Section 13.1(b)) is referred to herein as the "Fund Term."
[478|Normal] Section 13.2 — Events of Dissolution
[479|Normal] The Partnership shall be dissolved upon the first to occur of the following events:
[480|Normal] (a) the expiration of the Fund Term (including any extension thereof pursuant to Section 13.1(b));
[481|Normal] (b) the written consent of Partners holding at least seventy-five percent (75%) in Interest of all Partners;
[482|Normal] (c) the removal of the General Partner pursuant to Article X if no successor General Partner is elected within one hundred twenty (120) days following the effective date of such removal;
[483|Normal] (d) the entry of a judicial decree of dissolution under the DRULPA; or
[484|Normal] (e) the occurrence of any other event requiring the dissolution of the Partnership under the DRULPA that is not cured or waived in accordance with the DRULPA.
[485|Normal] The dissolution of the Partnership shall be effective on the date on which the applicable event occurs, but the Partnership shall not terminate until its affairs have been wound up and its assets distributed in accordance with this Agreement and the DRULPA.
[486|Normal] Section 13.3 — Winding Up
[487|Normal] (a) Upon dissolution of the Partnership, the General Partner (or, if there is no General Partner, a liquidating trustee appointed by a majority in Interest of all Limited Partners) shall proceed to wind up the affairs of the Partnership and to liquidate the assets of the Partnership in an orderly manner, consistent with maximizing value for the Partners.
[488|Normal] (b) The winding up of the Partnership shall include: (i) the sale or other disposition of all Portfolio Investments; (ii) the collection of all receivables; (iii) the payment (or provision for payment) of all debts, liabilities, and obligations of the Partnership; and (iv) the distribution of the remaining assets to the Partners in accordance with Section 13.4.
[489|Normal] (c) The General Partner (or liquidating trustee) shall cause the Accounting Firm (Graystone Whitaker LLP) to prepare a final accounting of the Partnership, including a final determination of each Partner's Capital Account, within one hundred twenty (120) days following the completion of the winding-up process.
[490|Normal] Section 13.4 — Distributions Upon Dissolution
[491|Normal] Upon dissolution of the Partnership, after payment (or provision for payment) of all debts, liabilities, and obligations of the Partnership and the establishment of such reserves for contingent liabilities as the General Partner (or liquidating trustee) deems reasonably necessary, the remaining assets of the Partnership shall be distributed to the Partners in the following order of priority:
[492|Normal] (a) First, to the payment of any remaining debts and liabilities of the Partnership (including amounts owed to Partners in their capacities as creditors of the Partnership);
[493|Normal] (b) Second, to the establishment of reasonable reserves for contingent liabilities, which reserves shall be distributed to the Partners upon resolution of such contingencies;
[494|Normal] (c) Third, to the Partners in accordance with the waterfall set forth in Section 7.2, applied on a cumulative, aggregate basis across all Realized Investments and all remaining Portfolio Investments (valued at fair market value for in-kind distributions), and after giving effect to the final Clawback obligation set forth in Section 7.6.
[495|Normal] Section 13.5 — Cancellation of Certificate
[496|Normal] Upon the completion of the winding up of the Partnership and the distribution of all assets of the Partnership to the Partners, the General Partner (or liquidating trustee) shall cause the Certificate to be cancelled by filing a certificate of cancellation with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, Division of Corporations, in accordance with the DRULPA.
[498|Normal] ARTICLE XIV — TRANSFERS OF PARTNERSHIP INTERESTS
[499|Normal] Section 14.1 — Restrictions on Transfer
[500|Normal] (a) No Limited Partner may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, encumber, or otherwise dispose of (each, a "Transfer") all or any portion of its Interest (or any economic or other rights therein) without the prior written consent of the General Partner, which consent may be withheld in the General Partner's sole and absolute discretion.
[501|Normal] (b) Any purported Transfer in violation of this Section 14.1 shall be null and void and of no force or effect, and the Partnership shall not recognize any such purported Transfer or admit any purported transferee as a Partner.
[502|Normal] (c) The restrictions on Transfer set forth in this Article XIV are intended to ensure compliance with applicable securities laws, to preserve the Partnership's tax classification, and to protect the interests of the Partners. Each Limited Partner acknowledges that these restrictions are reasonable and necessary for the foregoing purposes.
[503|Normal] Section 14.2 — Conditions to Transfer
[504|Normal] No Transfer of an Interest (or any portion thereof) shall be effective unless and until all of the following conditions have been satisfied:
[505|Normal] (a) the General Partner has consented to such Transfer in writing;
[506|Normal] (b) the transferee has demonstrated to the reasonable satisfaction of the General Partner that it meets the suitability requirements applicable to Limited Partners, including that it is an "accredited investor" within the meaning of Regulation D under the Securities Act and a "qualified purchaser" within the meaning of Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act of 1940;
[507|Normal] (c) the General Partner has received, at the expense of the transferring Limited Partner, a legal opinion from counsel reasonably satisfactory to the General Partner to the effect that such Transfer (i) is exempt from registration under the Securities Act and applicable state securities laws, and (ii) will not cause the Partnership to be treated as a "publicly traded partnership" within the meaning of Section 7704 of the Code or result in a termination of the Partnership under Section 708 of the Code;
[508|Normal] (d) the General Partner has received, at the expense of the transferring Limited Partner, a legal opinion from tax counsel reasonably satisfactory to the General Partner to the effect that such Transfer will not result in materially adverse tax consequences to the Partnership or any Partner;
[509|Normal] (e) the transferring Limited Partner and the transferee have executed and delivered to the General Partner such instruments and documents as the General Partner may reasonably require to effectuate such Transfer, including a Transfer Agreement in substantially the form of Schedule F;
[510|Normal] (f) all costs and expenses incurred by the Partnership in connection with such Transfer (including legal fees and administrative expenses) have been borne by the transferring Limited Partner; and
[511|Normal] (g) the aggregate Interest being Transferred has a fair market value of not less than five million dollars ($5,000,000) (or such lesser amount as the General Partner may approve in its discretion).
[512|Normal] Section 14.3 — Substitute Limited Partners
[513|Normal] (a) A transferee of an Interest (or any portion thereof) may be admitted to the Partnership as a substitute Limited Partner only with the prior written consent of the General Partner (which consent may be withheld in the General Partner's sole discretion) and upon satisfaction of all conditions set forth in Section 14.2.
[514|Normal] (b) Upon admission as a substitute Limited Partner, the transferee shall succeed to the Interest (or portion thereof) of the transferring Limited Partner and shall assume all obligations and liabilities of the transferring Limited Partner with respect to such Interest (including the obligation to fund unfunded Capital Commitments).
[515|Normal] (c) The transferring Limited Partner shall be released from its obligations under this Agreement only to the extent of the unfunded Capital Commitment assumed by the transferee. The transferring Limited Partner shall remain liable for any obligations that accrued prior to the date of Transfer.
[516|Normal] Section 14.4 — Transfers by Operation of Law
[517|Normal] (a) In the event of the death, bankruptcy, insolvency, or legal incapacity of any Limited Partner (or, in the case of a Limited Partner that is an entity, the dissolution, liquidation, or termination of such entity), the legal representative, successor, or assign of such Limited Partner shall be bound by the terms of this Agreement and shall succeed to the Interest of such Limited Partner, subject to compliance with the Transfer conditions set forth in Section 14.2 (to the extent applicable).
[518|Normal] (b) The Partnership shall recognize the Transfer of an Interest by operation of law upon receipt of satisfactory evidence of such Transfer and compliance with such conditions as the General Partner may reasonably impose.
[519|Normal] Section 14.5 — Transfers by the General Partner
[520|Normal] (a) The General Partner may not Transfer its general partnership Interest in the Partnership without the prior written consent of Limited Partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) in Interest of all Limited Partners; provided that the General Partner may, without such consent, Transfer its general partnership Interest to an Affiliate of the General Partner, so long as such Affiliate assumes all obligations and liabilities of the General Partner under this Agreement.
[521|Normal] (b) Any change of control of the General Partner (whether by merger, sale of equity interests, or otherwise) shall be treated as a Transfer of the General Partner's Interest for purposes of this Section 14.5.
[523|Normal] ARTICLE XV — SIDE LETTERS AND MOST FAVORED NATION RIGHTS
[524|Normal] Section 15.1 — Side Letters
[525|Normal] (a) The General Partner may enter into Side Letters or other written agreements with any Limited Partner that have the effect of establishing rights under, or modifying, supplementing, or waiving the terms of, this Agreement with respect to such Limited Partner.
[526|Normal] (b) Side Letters may address, among other things: fee discounts or fee waivers, enhanced or supplemental reporting obligations, co-investment rights or preferences, excuse rights for specified categories of investments, enhanced transfer rights, opt-out rights for specific investments, and other accommodations reasonably requested by a Limited Partner.
[527|Normal] (c) Side Letters are binding only on the Partnership and the relevant Limited Partner and do not modify this Agreement with respect to other Limited Partners, except to the extent of MFN elections pursuant to Section 15.3.
[528|Normal] Section 15.2 — Disclosure of Side Letters
[529|Normal] (a) The General Partner shall disclose the existence (but not necessarily the specific terms) of all Side Letters entered into with Limited Partners to all other Limited Partners.
[530|Normal] (b) Upon written request, the General Partner shall provide any Limited Partner with a summary of the material economic terms granted in Side Letters entered into with other Limited Partners (redacted to remove the identity of the relevant Limited Partner, if requested by such Limited Partner), to the extent that such terms are eligible for MFN election pursuant to Section 15.3.
[531|Normal] Section 15.3 — Most Favored Nation ("MFN") Elections
[532|Normal] (a) Within thirty (30) days after the Final Closing, the General Partner shall provide each Limited Partner with a summary of the material terms of all Side Letters entered into with other Limited Partners (the "MFN Summary").
[533|Normal] (b) Each Limited Partner shall have the right, within thirty (30) days of receiving the MFN Summary (the "MFN Election Period"), to elect to receive the benefit of any or all terms contained in any Side Letter entered into with any other Limited Partner of equal or smaller Capital Commitment (each such election, an "MFN Election").
[534|Normal] (c) MFN Elections shall be effective as of the Final Closing.
[535|Normal] (d) The General Partner shall confirm each MFN Election in writing within fifteen (15) Business Days of receipt of such election, and shall promptly prepare and deliver to the electing Limited Partner a supplemental Side Letter reflecting the elected terms.
[537|Normal] ARTICLE XVI — EXCUSE AND EXCLUSION
[538|Normal] Section 16.1 — Excuse Rights
[539|Normal] (a) A Limited Partner may request to be excused from participating in a particular Portfolio Investment if such Limited Partner demonstrates to the reasonable satisfaction of the Advisory Committee that participation in such Portfolio Investment would cause:
[540|Normal] (i) a violation of applicable law, regulation, or order of any governmental authority having jurisdiction over such Limited Partner;
[541|Normal] (ii) a material adverse tax consequence to such Limited Partner (including, for the avoidance of doubt, the imposition of unrelated business taxable income ("UBTI") or effectively connected income ("ECI") for tax-exempt or non-U.S. Limited Partners); or
[542|Normal] (iii) a conflict with such Limited Partner's governing documents, charter, bylaws, published investment policies, or fiduciary obligations.
[543|Normal] (b) Excuse requests shall be submitted in writing to the General Partner within ten (10) Business Days of receipt of the relevant Capital Call or investment notification. Each excuse request shall include a reasonably detailed explanation of the basis for the request and such supporting documentation as the General Partner or the Advisory Committee may reasonably require.
[544|Normal] (c) The Advisory Committee shall review excuse requests and shall grant or deny such requests in its reasonable discretion within fifteen (15) Business Days of receipt thereof. The Advisory Committee may consult with the General Partner and Legal Counsel in connection with its review of excuse requests. The decision of the Advisory Committee shall be final and binding on the requesting Limited Partner.
[545|Normal] (d) If an excuse request is granted, the excused Limited Partner shall not be required to fund its pro rata share of the relevant Portfolio Investment, and such excused amount shall be reallocated in accordance with Section 16.3.
[546|Normal] Section 16.2 — Effect of Excuse on Commitments and Fees
[547|Normal] (a) Excused amounts shall reduce the excused Limited Partner's Capital Commitment for purposes of calculating the Management Fee under Section 5.1. The Management Fee payable with respect to the excused Limited Partner shall be recalculated based on such Limited Partner's reduced effective Capital Commitment (i.e., the Capital Commitment minus all excused amounts).
[548|Normal] (b) Excused amounts shall not be available for recycling by the General Partner pursuant to Section 6.7.
[549|Normal] (c) The excused Limited Partner's Percentage Interest with respect to the excused Portfolio Investment shall be zero; its share of Net Profits, Net Losses, and Distributions attributable to such excused Portfolio Investment shall be zero.
[550|Normal] Section 16.3 — Reallocation of Excused Amounts

[561|Normal] (c) Notwithstanding Section 17.1(a), the General Partner may, without the consent of any Limited Partner, make ministerial, administrative, or clarifying amendments to this Agreement that do not adversely affect the rights or obligations of any Limited Partner, including amendments to: (i) reflect the admission of additional or substitute Limited Partners; (ii) correct typographical errors, ambiguities, or inconsistencies; (iii) update the names, addresses, or other identifying information of the Partners; (iv) comply with applicable law or regulatory requirements; or (v) reflect changes that have been approved by the Advisory Committee. Any such amendment shall be promptly communicated to all Limited Partners.
[562|Normal] Section 17.2 — Governing Law

The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three (3) arbitrators, one appointed by each party and the third appointed by the two party-appointed arbitrators. [596|Normal] Section 17.10 — Indemnification
[597|Normal] (a) The Partnership shall indemnify and hold harmless the General Partner, the Management Company, their respective Affiliates, and each of their respective members, partners, officers, directors, employees, and agents (collectively, the "Indemnified Persons") from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses), judgments, fines, settlements, and other amounts (collectively, "Losses") arising from any claims, demands, actions, suits, or proceedings (whether civil, criminal, administrative, or investigative) relating to the Partnership's activities or the performance by such Indemnified Person of its duties hereunder; provided, however, that no Indemnified Person shall be entitled to indemnification hereunder to the extent that such Losses result from such Indemnified Person's fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or material breach of this Agreement.
[598|Normal] (b) Expenses incurred by an Indemnified Person in defending any claim, action, suit, or proceeding for which such Indemnified Person is entitled to indemnification under this Section 17.10 shall be advanced by the Partnership pending the final disposition of such claim, action, suit, or proceeding, upon receipt by the Partnership of an undertaking by or on behalf of such Indemnified Person to repay such amounts if it is ultimately determined that such Indemnified Person is not entitled to indemnification hereunder.
[599|Normal] (c) The indemnification provided by this Section 17.10 shall not be exclusive of any other rights to which an Indemnified Person may be entitled under any other agreement, insurance policy, or as a matter of law. The General Partner may cause the Partnership to obtain and maintain directors' and officers' liability insurance, errors and omissions insurance, and such other insurance coverage as the General Partner deems necessary or appropriate for the protection of the Indemnified Persons, at the Partnership's expense.
[600|Normal] (d) The indemnification and advancement of expenses provided by this Section 17.10 shall survive the dissolution and termination of the Partnership and shall continue in full force and effect with respect to any Indemnified Person who has ceased to serve in such capacity, with respect to acts or omissions occurring during such Person's service.
[601|Normal] Section 17.11 — Exculpation; Standard of Care
[602|Normal] (a) No Indemnified Person shall be liable to the Partnership or to any Partner for any act or omission performed or omitted by such Indemnified Person in good faith and in a manner reasonably believed to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Partnership; provided, however, that no Indemnified Person shall be exculpated from liability for any act or omission constituting fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or a material breach of this Agreement.
[603|Normal] (b) The General Partner shall not be liable to the Partnership or to any Partner for errors of judgment or for any investment losses sustained by the Partnership, provided that the General Partner has acted in good faith and in accordance with the standards set forth in this Agreement. The Partners acknowledge that investments in Portfolio Companies involve a high degree of risk and that losses are an inherent part of the Partnership's investment program.
[604|Normal] (c) The General Partner may rely in good faith upon the opinions, reports, and statements of Legal Counsel (Ashford Blake LLP), the Accounting Firm (Graystone Whitaker LLP), the Valuation Firm (Ridgepoint Valuations Inc.), the Fund Administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC), and other professional advisors retained by the Partnership, and such reliance shall not constitute gross negligence or willful misconduct.
[605|Normal] Section 17.12 — Successors and Assigns
[606|Normal] This Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors, permitted assigns, heirs, executors, administrators, and legal representatives.
[607|Normal] Section 17.13 — Third-Party Beneficiaries
[608|Normal] Except as expressly provided herein with respect to Indemnified Persons (who are intended third-party beneficiaries of Sections 17.10 and 17.11), nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any Person other than the parties hereto any rights, benefits, or remedies of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement.
[609|Normal] Section 17.14 — Waiver of Partition
[610|Normal] Each Partner hereby waives any right to partition the assets of the Partnership or to file a complaint or institute any proceeding for partition of the assets of the Partnership.
[611|Normal] Section 17.15 — Construction
[612|Normal] (a) The headings and captions contained in this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement.
[613|Normal] (b) Unless the context otherwise requires: (i) the term "including" (and correlative terms such as "include" and "includes") means "including, without limitation"; (ii) words in the singular include the plural, and words in the plural include the singular; (iii) words importing the masculine gender include the feminine and neuter genders, and vice versa; (iv) references to any statute or law include all amendments, modifications, and replacements thereof, and all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder; and (v) references to "Sections," "Articles," "Schedules," and "Exhibits" are to sections, articles, schedules, and exhibits of this Agreement unless otherwise indicated.
[614|Normal] (c) The parties hereto have participated jointly in the negotiation and drafting of this Agreement. In the event of any ambiguity or question of intent or interpretation, this Agreement shall be construed as if drafted jointly by all parties, and no presumption or burden of proof shall arise favoring or disfavoring any party by virtue of the authorship of any provision of this Agreement.
[615|Normal] Section 17.16 — Legal Counsel
[616|Normal] (a) Each Limited Partner acknowledges and agrees that Ashford Blake LLP has acted as counsel to the General Partner and the Management Company (and not to any Limited Partner) in connection with the formation of the Partnership, the negotiation and preparation of this Agreement, and the offering of the Interests. Ashford Blake LLP does not represent, and has no attorney-client relationship with, any Limited Partner.
[617|Normal] (b) Each Limited Partner is advised to retain its own independent legal, tax, and financial advisors in connection with its investment in the Partnership and the review of this Agreement.
[618|Normal] (c) Ashford Blake LLP may continue to represent the General Partner and/or the Management Company in any matter involving the Partnership, including in connection with any dispute or controversy between the General Partner and one or more Limited Partners, and each Limited Partner hereby consents to such continued representation and waives any conflict of interest arising therefrom.
[619|Normal] Section 17.17 — Compliance with Laws; ERISA
[620|Normal] (a) The Partnership shall conduct its affairs so as not to be required to register as an "investment company" under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the "Investment Company Act"). The General Partner shall not take any action that would cause the Partnership to be required to register under the Investment Company Act and shall take such actions as may be necessary or appropriate to ensure the availability of one or more exemptions from registration thereunder (including the exemptions provided by Sections 3(c)(1) and 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act).
[621|Normal] (b) The Partnership shall operate such that less than twenty-five percent (25%) of the value of each class of equity interests in the Partnership is held by "benefit plan investors" within the meaning of Section 3(42) of ERISA and 29 C.F.R. §2510.3-101 (as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA). The General Partner shall monitor the composition of the Partnership's investors and shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure compliance with the foregoing limitation, including limiting the amount of Capital Commitments that may be accepted from benefit plan investors.
[622|Normal] (c) Each Limited Partner shall make such representations and warranties to the Partnership as the General Partner may reasonably require in connection with applicable anti-money laundering laws and regulations, including the USA PATRIOT Act and regulations administered by OFAC. Each Limited Partner represents and warrants that it is not, and is not owned or controlled by, a Person that is: (i) the subject of any sanctions administered or enforced by OFAC, the United Nations Security Council, the European Union, or Her Majesty's Treasury; or (ii) located, organized, or resident in a country or territory that is the subject of comprehensive sanctions (including Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and the Crimea region of Ukraine).
[623|Normal] Section 17.18 — Force Majeure
[624|Normal] Neither the General Partner nor any Limited Partner shall be liable for any failure to perform or delay in performing any obligation under this Agreement to the extent that such failure or delay is caused by or results from acts of God, fire, flood, earthquake, pandemic, epidemic, war, terrorism, civil unrest, strikes, lockouts, governmental actions, sanctions, embargoes, or other events beyond the reasonable control of such party (each, a "Force Majeure Event"). The affected party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of any Force Majeure Event and to resume performance of its obligations as soon as practicable.

[653|Normal] Assumptions:

[655|Normal] •  Gross Disposition Proceeds from Investment A: $200,000,000

[662|Normal] Step 1 — Return of Capital (Section 7.2(a)):
[663|Normal] $100,000,000 distributed to the Limited Partners (pro rata), representing the return of their Capital Contributions attributable to Investment A.
[664|Normal] Remaining Net Proceeds: $200,000,000 – $100,000,000 = $100,000,000
[665|Normal] Step 2 — Preferred Return (Section 7.2(b)):
[666|Normal] The Preferred Return is calculated at seven percent (7%) per annum, compounded quarterly, on the Limited Partners' Unreturned Capital Contributions of $100,000,000 over a holding period of 4 years (16 quarters):
[667|Normal] Preferred Return = $100,000,000 × (1 + 0.07/4)^16 – $100,000,000
[668|Normal] Preferred Return = $100,000,000 × (1.0175)^16 – $100,000,000
[669|Normal] Preferred Return = $100,000,000 × 1.319929 – $100,000,000
[670|Normal] Preferred Return = $131,992,903 – $100,000,000
[671|Normal] Preferred Return = $31,992,903
[672|Normal] $31,992,903 distributed to the Limited Partners (pro rata).
[673|Normal] Remaining Net Proceeds: $100,000,000 – $31,992,903 = $68,007,097
[674|Normal] Step 3 — GP Catch-Up (Section 7.2(c)):
[675|Normal] The GP Catch-Up is distributed eighty percent (80%) to the General Partner and twenty percent (20%) to the Limited Partners until the General Partner has received an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of cumulative amounts distributed under Steps 2 and 3.

[691|Normal] Netting Reserve Illustration (Section 7.4):
[692|Normal] Assume that, at the time of the Distribution related to Investment A, the Partnership also holds Investment B, which has an unrealized loss of $15,000,000 (i.e., the fair market value of Investment B is $15,000,000 below cost). Assume further that there are no other unrealized gains in the remaining portfolio.
[693|Normal] Under Section 7.4, the General Partner would calculate the Netting Reserve as follows:
[694|Normal] •  Net unrealized losses across remaining portfolio: $15,000,000
[695|Normal] •  Netting Reserve Amount: 20% × $15,000,000 = $3,000,000
[696|Normal] The General Partner would withhold $3,000,000 from the Carried Interest otherwise distributable to the General Partner in Steps 3 and 4 above and deposit such amount in the Carried Interest Escrow. The remaining Carried Interest ($20,000,000 – $3,000,000 = $17,000,000) would be distributed to the General Partner (subject to the 25% escrow under Section 7.3, applied to the full $20,000,000 of Carried Interest before the Netting Reserve adjustment).
[697|Normal] The Netting Reserve Amount would be re-evaluated at each subsequent Distribution Date. If Investment B is subsequently realized at or above cost, the Netting Reserve Amount of $3,000,000 (plus any interest earned thereon) would be released to the General Partner from the Carried Interest Escrow, subject to Advisory Committee consent.

 "the Investment Period shall be deemed permanently terminated, and the provisions of this Agreement applicable following the expiration or termination of the Investment Period (including Sections 4.1(d), 5.1(b), 6.2(c), and 6.7(c)) shall apply.")
NOTE(P[390], "Section 9.2(c)–(d)", "Reinstatement vote",

Section 7.2 --- Distribution Waterfall (Whole-Fund)]{.underline}**
All Net Proceeds and other amounts available for distribution by the Partnership (after deducting Partnership Expenses and reasonable reserves established in accordance with Section 7.1(a)) shall be aggregated and distributed among the Partners on a cumulative, whole-fund basis (and not on a deal-by-deal or investment-by-investment basis) in the following order of priority:
**(a) Return of** **Capital.** First, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Capital Contributions, until each Limited Partner has received cumulative Distributions equal to the aggregate amount of all Capital Contributions made by such Limited Partner to the Partnership (including Capital Contributions applied to Management Fees, Organizational Expenses, and Partnership Expenses).
**(b) Preferred** **Return.** Second, one hundred percent (100%) to the Limited Partners, pro rata in proportion to their respective Capital Contributions, until each Limited Partner has received cumulative Distributions under this clause (b) equal to a cumulative preferred return of eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually (and not quarterly), on such Limited Partner's Unreturned Capital Contributions, calculated from the date each such Capital Contribution was made through the date of the relevant Distribution (the \"Preferred Return\"). For purposes of this clause (b), \"Unreturned Capital Contributions\" means Capital Contributions that have not been returned pursuant to clause (a) above.
**(c) GP Catch-Up.** Third, one hundred percent (100%) to the General Partner until the General Partner has received cumulative Distributions under this clause (c) equal to twenty percent (20%) of the sum of (x) all amounts distributed pursuant to clause (b) of this Section 7.2 and (y) all amounts distributed pursuant to this clause (c) (the \"GP Catch-Up Amount\"). For the avoidance of doubt, at the completion of the GP Catch-Up the General Partner will have received an amount X such that X = 20% × (Preferred Return + X), i.e., X = 25% of the aggregate Preferred Return distributed under clause (b), with the result that the General Partner will have received twenty percent (20%) of all amounts distributed pursuant to clauses (b) and (c) of this Section 7.2 combined.
**(d)** **Residual** **Split.** Fourth, thereafter, eighty percent (80%) to the Limited Partners (pro rata in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests) and twenty percent (20%) to the General Partner.
For purposes of determining the General Partner's entitlement to Carried Interest under this Section 7.2, see also Section 7.3 (Escrow of Carried Interest Distributions) and Section 7.6 (Clawback Obligation). No deal-by-deal escrow, interim clawback, or loss carry-forward or netting reserve shall apply to Distributions under this Section 7.2. The General Partner\'s share of distributions under Sections 7.2(c) and 7.2(d) constitutes the \"Carried Interest\" payable to the General Partner hereunder. Carried Interest is payable solely from Distributions and shall not be separately invoiced or charged. \[For purposes of this Section 7.2, the General Partner (and its Affiliates) shall participate in Distributions under clauses (a), (b), and (d) in respect of the GP Commitment as if it were a Limited Partner, and amounts so distributed in respect of the GP Commitment shall not constitute Carried Interest.\]
*[**\[Partner Note 16 --- Whole-fund waterfall:** The deal-by-deal waterfall has been converted to a whole-fund (European) structure with a 100% GP catch-up, and the Netting Reserve (former Section 7.4) and Interim Clawback (former Section 7.5) have been deleted and marked \"\[Reserved\]\" to preserve cross-references. Points for review: (i) the 30% Clawback Escrow in Section 7.3 is retained because Term Sheet Section 7.3 expressly requires it; we read the Term Sheet's \"no deal-by-deal escrow mechanics\" as directed at the Fund III Netting Reserve escrow, but please confirm; (ii) the Term Sheet contains no early-carry or \"fair value cushion\" test, so no Carried Interest is distributable until all Capital Contributions (including those applied to fees and expenses) and the full Preferred Return have been distributed; (iii) Tax Distributions (Section 7.9) remain advances against Distributions under Section 7.2; (iv) the catch-up is expressed as 20% of amounts distributed under clauses (b) and (c), consistent with Term Sheet Section 6.2; and (v) see the Partner Note at Section 3.1(b) regarding the GP Commitment.**\]**]{.mark}*
**[Section 7.3 --- Escrow of Carried Interest Distributions]{.underline}**
**(a)** Notwithstanding Sections 7.2(c) and 7.2(d), thirty percent (30%) of all Carried Interest distributions otherwise payable to the General Partner pursuant to Sections 7.2(c) and 7.2(d) shall not be distributed to the General Partner but shall instead be deposited into the Carried Interest Escrow account maintained by the Escrow Agent (Northbrook Trust Company) pursuant to the Escrow Agreement. The remaining seventy percent (70%) of such Carried Interest distributions shall be distributed to the General Partner in accordance with Section 7.2.
**(b)** Amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow shall be released to the General Partner upon the final liquidation of the Partnership, to the extent not required to satisfy the Clawback obligation set forth in Section 7.6 (and after giving effect to any amounts required to satisfy such Clawback obligation).
*[**\[Partner Note 17 --- Escrow release:** Term Sheet Section 7.3 provides for release of the Clawback Escrow only upon final liquidation. We have deleted the Fund III early-release mechanic (GP determination plus LPAC consent) and the corresponding LPAC consent right in former Section 11.3(d). The General Partner may wish to negotiate an interim release where escrow balances materially exceed any projected clawback, but that would be a departure from the Term Sheet.**\]**]{.mark}*
**(c)** Amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow shall be invested in short-term United States Treasury obligations or money market funds, as directed by the General Partner.
**(d)** Interest and other income earned on amounts held in the Carried Interest Escrow shall be credited to the General Partner\'s account within the escrow but shall remain in the Carried Interest Escrow until such amounts are released to the General Partner pursuant to Section 7.3(b) or applied to satisfy the Clawback obligation pursuant to Section 7.6.
**(e)** A summary of the terms of the Escrow Agreement is set forth in Exhibit C.

The \"Key Persons\" for purposes of this Agreement shall be Richard Holloway (Founder and Chief Executive Officer) and Catherine Yuen (Co-Managing Partner). The \"Senior Partners\" for purposes of this Agreement shall be Thomas Agarwal, Danielle Matsuda, Erik Sorensen, Monica Hale, and Jonathan Trevino.
**(b)** A \"Key Person Event\" shall occur upon the earliest to occur of the following:
**(A) Tier 1 Trigger.** Richard Holloway ceases to devote Substantially All of his business time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership \[and the Management Company and its Affiliates (including the Predecessor Fund)\]; or
**(B) Tier 2 Trigger.** Both of the following conditions are satisfied: (1) Catherine Yuen ceases to devote Substantially All of her business time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership \[and the Management Company and its Affiliates (including the Predecessor Fund)\]; and (2) fewer than three (3) of the five (5) Senior Partners remain actively involved in the affairs of the Partnership.
For the avoidance of doubt: (x) the cessation described in clause (A) above with respect to Richard Holloway alone shall constitute a Key Person Event, regardless of the status of Catherine Yuen or any Senior Partner; (y) the cessation described in clause (B)(1) above with respect to Catherine Yuen alone shall not constitute a Key Person Event if at least three (3) Senior Partners remain actively involved in the affairs of the Partnership; and (z) the departure of one or more Senior Partners alone (without the cessation described in clause (B)(1) above with respect to Catherine Yuen) shall not constitute a Key Person Event. A Key Person Event under clause (B) shall occur on the date on which both conditions described therein are first satisfied, regardless of the order in which they occur.
**(c)** For purposes of this Section 9.1, a Key Person shall not be deemed to have ceased to devote Substantially All of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership, and a Key Person Event shall not be deemed to have occurred, solely by reason of:
> \(i\) a temporary absence due to illness, injury, or disability for a period not exceeding one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days;
>
> \(ii\) reasonable vacation time consistent with the Key Person\'s past practice; or
>
> \(iii\) service on up to three (3) outside boards of directors of entities that do not compete, directly or indirectly, with the Partnership\'s investment program.
**(d) For the avoidance of doubt, (i) the death, permanent disability, or voluntary resignation of Richard Holloway from his position with the Management Company shall constitute a Key Person Event, and (ii) the death, permanent disability, or voluntary resignation of Catherine Yuen from her position with the Management Company shall constitute a cessation for purposes of Section 9.1(b)(B)(1), but shall constitute a Key Person Event only if the condition set forth in Section 9.1(b)(B)(2) is also satisfied.**
**(e)** A Senior Partner shall cease to be \"actively involved\" in the affairs of the Partnership upon \[such Senior Partner's death, permanent disability, resignation, or termination of employment with the Management Company and its Affiliates, or such Senior Partner ceasing to devote \[a majority\] of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership and its Affiliates\].
*[**\[Partner Note 19 --- Two-tier Key Person:** The two-tier Term Sheet trigger is implemented in Section 9.1(b), including the Term Sheet's avoidance-of-doubt examples (x)--(z). Open points: (i) the Term Sheet tests time commitment to \"the affairs of the Fund,\" which read literally is inconsistent with the Key Persons' continuing responsibilities to the Predecessor Fund (whose term runs to at least 2031) and the Management Company; we have bracketed broader language, and the anchors may require a split formulation (e.g., Substantially All to the Partnership and its Affiliates, with a minimum allocation to the Partnership); (ii) \"actively involved\" is undefined in the Term Sheet; a bracketed definition is in Section 9.1(e); (iii) the Fund III carve-outs in Section 9.1(c) (180-day disability, vacation, three outside boards) are retained although the Term Sheet is silent, and LPs may view 180 days as long; (iv) we have clarified that a Tier 2 event occurs when both limbs are first satisfied, in either order; and (v) see the Partner Notes at Section 1.1 (\"Substantially All\" and \"Senior Partners\").**\]**]{.mark}*
**[Section 9.2 --- Consequences of a Key Person Event]{.underline}**
**(a)** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the Investment Period shall be automatically suspended as of the date of such Key Person Event (the period of such suspension, the \"Suspension Period\").
**(b)** During the Suspension Period, the General Partner shall not make any new Portfolio Investments on behalf of the Partnership or issue any Capital Calls for the purpose of making new Portfolio Investments; provided that the General Partner may issue Capital Calls for, and may, (i) \[fund investments pursuant to binding commitments entered into prior to the date of the Key Person Event,\] (ii) make follow-on investments in existing Portfolio Companies \[that the General Partner determines in good faith are necessary or advisable to protect, preserve, or enhance the value of existing Portfolio Investments\], and (iii) pay Management Fees, Partnership Expenses, and other fees, expenses, and obligations of the Partnership from available funds or unfunded Capital Commitments.
*[**\[Partner Note 20 --- Permitted activity during Suspension Period:** The Term Sheet permits capital calls during the Suspension Period for \"fees, expenses, and follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies,\" without the Fund III value-protection qualifier on follow-ons and without any express reference to investments under binding commitments entered into before the Key Person Event. Both are bracketed. [Section 10.3 --- Voting Procedures for Removal

> • Aggregate Net Proceeds: \$200,000,000
>
> • Holding Period: 4 years (all Capital Contributions assumed made on a single date and all Distributions made on the fourth (4th) anniversary thereof)
>
> • Preferred Return Rate: eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually
>
> • GP Catch-Up: one hundred percent (100%) to the General Partner until the General Partner has received 20% of cumulative amounts distributed under Steps 2 and 3
>
> • Residual Split: eighty percent (80%) to the Limited Partners, twenty percent (20%) to the General Partner
Step 1 --- Return of Capital (Section 7.2(a)):
\$100,000,000 distributed to the Limited Partners (pro rata), representing the return of their Capital Contributions to the Partnership.
Remaining Net Proceeds: \$200,000,000 -- \$100,000,000 = \$100,000,000
Step 2 --- Preferred Return (Section 7.2(b)):
The Preferred Return is calculated at eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually, on the Limited Partners\' Unreturned Capital Contributions of \$100,000,000 over a holding period of 4 years:
Preferred Return = \$100,000,000 × (1 + 0.08)\^4 -- \$100,000,000
Preferred Return = \$100,000,000 × (1.08)\^4 -- \$100,000,000
Preferred Return = \$100,000,000 × 1.36048896 -- \$100,000,000
Preferred Return = \$136,048,896 -- \$100,000,000
Preferred Return = \$36,048,896
\$36,048,896 distributed to the Limited Partners (pro rata).
Remaining Net Proceeds: \$100,000,000 -- \$36,048,896 = \$63,951,104
Step 3 --- GP Catch-Up (Section 7.2(c)):
The GP Catch-Up is distributed one hundred percent (100%) to the General Partner until the General Partner has received an amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of cumulative amounts distributed under Steps 2 and 3.
Let X = total amount distributed in Step 3.
GP receives 100% of X. The condition is:
X = 0.20 × (\$36,048,896 + X)
X = \$7,209,779 + 0.20X
0.80X = \$7,209,779
X = \$9,012,224 (i.e., 25% × \$36,048,896)
GP receives: 100% × \$9,012,224 = \$9,012,224 LPs receive: \$0
Verification: GP has received \$9,012,224 out of total Steps 2 + 3 of \$36,048,896 + \$9,012,224 = \$45,061,120. GP percentage: \$9,012,224 / \$45,061,120 = 20.0%.
Remaining Net Proceeds: \$63,951,104 -- \$9,012,224 = \$54,938,880
Step 4 --- Residual Split (Section 7.2(d)):
Remaining Net Proceeds of \$54,938,880 distributed:
LPs receive: 80% × \$54,938,880 = \$43,951,104 GP receives: 20% × \$54,938,880 = \$10,987,776

  Step                LPs Receive     GP Receives    Total
  ----------------------- ------------------- ------------------ -------------------
  1\. Return of Capital   \$100,000,000       \$0                \$100,000,000
  2\. Preferred Return    \$36,048,896        \$0                \$36,048,896
  3\. GP Catch-Up         \$0                 \$9,012,224        \$9,012,224
  4\. Residual Split      \$43,951,104        \$10,987,776       \$54,938,880
  Total               \$180,000,000   \$20,000,000   \$200,000,000
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Verification: The General Partner receives \$20,000,000, which equals twenty percent (20%) of the total Net Profits of \$100,000,000 (\$200,000,000 Net Proceeds less \$100,000,000 return of capital).
Clawback Escrow and After-Tax Clawback Illustration (Sections 7.3 and 7.6):
Of the \$20,000,000 of Carried Interest distributable to the General Partner in Steps 3 and 4 above, thirty percent (30%), or \$6,000,000, would be deposited in the Clawback Escrow maintained by the Escrow Agent pursuant to Section 7.3, and the remaining \$14,000,000 would be distributed to the General Partner.
Assume further that, upon the final liquidation of the Partnership, the General Partner is determined to have received cumulative Carried Interest exceeding twenty percent (20%) of cumulative Net Profits (after the return of all Capital Contributions and payment of the Preferred Return, on a whole-fund basis) by \$5,000,000. Under Section 7.6(b), the Clawback Amount would be calculated as follows:
> • Excess Carried Interest: \$5,000,000
>
> • Clawback Amount: \$5,000,000 × (1 -- 0.45) = \$2,750,000
The Clawback Amount of \$2,750,000 would first be satisfied from amounts held in the Clawback Escrow (\$6,000,000, plus income earned thereon), and the balance of the Clawback Escrow (\$3,250,000, plus any such income) would be released to the General Partner upon the final liquidation of the Partnership.
No Netting Reserve, interim clawback, or deal-by-deal escrow applies under the whole-fund waterfall.
